title: Not all AI-assisted programming is vibe coding (but vibe coding rocks)
description: Simon Willison clarifies the definition of 'vibe coding' (coined by Andrej Karpathy) - building software with an LLM without reviewing the code it writes. He emphasizes this is different from responsible AI-assisted programming where developers review, test, and understand the code. Willison argues vibe coding is valuable for low-stakes projects and helping beginners learn, but warns about security, privacy, and cost considerations. He believes vibe coding can lower barriers to programming and help experienced developers build intuition about LLM capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Ask HN: Anyone struggling to get value out of coding LLMs?
description: Hacker News discussion where developers share mixed experiences with LLM coding tools. Participants note that while LLMs are great as code suggestion tools for completing lines and functions, they struggle with delivering whole features. The conversation highlights the gap between expectations and reality for AI coding assistants.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Ask HN: Go deep into AI/LLMs or just use them as tools?
description: Hacker News discussion on whether developers should deeply specialize in AI/LLMs or simply use them as tools. Commenters note that LLMs have changed how we code, but agentic coding ('vibe coding') currently produces mixed results. The conversation explores the balance between understanding AI internals versus practical application.
author: Hacker News Community

title: A few random notes from Claude coding quite a bit last few weeks
description: Andrej Karpathy shares insights from extensive experience coding with Claude, noting the shift from 80% manual+autocomplete coding and 20% agents to a much higher reliance on AI coding agents. Discusses the rapid evolution of LLM coding capabilities and their impact on development workflows.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: After months of coding with LLMs, I'm going back to using my brain
description: Hacker News discussion on a reflection about LLM coding experiences. The conversation explores trade-offs of relying on LLMs, noting they excel at generating and updating code based on context and prompts, but discussing when developers should rely on their own expertise versus AI assistance.
author: Hacker News Community

title: How I write software with LLMs
description: Discussion about limitations of AI in writing large programs, noting that AI cannot write a 100k line program on its own without external guardrails otherwise it spins out. Explores the current boundaries of LLM coding capabilities and the need for human oversight.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Adding AI-generated descriptions to my tools collection
description: Simon Willison documents using Claude 3.7 Sonnet to automatically generate descriptions for 78 HTML+JavaScript tools in his tools collection. He created a script that processes each tool and generates 2-3 sentence documentation, costing $0.94 total (283,528 input tokens, 6,010 output tokens). The system tracks commit hashes to regenerate documentation when tools are updated. Willison reflects on this as 'the single largest chunk of AI-generated text' he's published on the indexable web.
author: Simon Willison
